tldr: Lilian Weng published "Harness Engineering for Self-Improvement" on July 4, tracing recursive self-improvement (RSI) back to I. J. Good's 1965 "ultraintelligent machine" concept. The essay surveys roughly 35 papers on the harness and scaffolding layer that lets models improve themselves.
whats_new: AINews' July 8 daily digest summarized Weng's harness-engineering survey four days after she published it, carrying the essay to a wider daily-reader audience via latent.space.
why_it_matters: It's a single curated map of current RSI/harness-engineering research — worth checking before a platform team builds new self-improvement scaffolding from scratch.

beats.headline: Weng publishes the harness-engineering survey
beats.summary: Frames RSI's history from I. J. Good's 1965 "ultraintelligent machine" through today's harness/scaffolding techniques.

beats.headline: AINews digest summarizes the essay for a wider audience
beats.summary: latent.space's daily AINews roundup condenses the 35-paper survey four days later.

open_questions: Does Weng's essay propose new evaluation criteria for self-improving harnesses, or mainly catalog existing techniques?
Will other researchers or outlets build on or respond to this survey?
take_for_builders: Treat this essay as a current literature map for self-improving agent harnesses — check it against your own scaffolding before adding new self-improvement machinery.
